metadata.title: sliced wood coasters
metadata.description:
** No narration in this video. CC enabled to describe process. **

Natural wood beverage coasters made from thinly sliced tree branches. Stylish and fun to make, these coasters are a great addition to any home, and make great gifts!

Dry tree branches were chopped up on a tabletop band saw into small pucks, which were then glued to a thin sheet of plywood. The pucks were staggered and were glued to overhang the edge of the plywood on three sides, leaving the fourth side straight as a reference for the table saw fence. 

Once the glue had dried overnight, the straight edge of the plywood was referenced to the table saw fence and planks were cut. To make the surface level a router was used as a planer. Setting the router base on a wide sled which rides on temporary rails. The planks were set between the rails with hot glue, then the router was lower after every pass to trim the wood down to a consistent height. The planks were easy pried up after planing. 

Using a cross cut sled, the level planks were cut square. Each was finished with Teak Oil to give a nice color and finish. Rubber pads were placed on the underside to stop them from sliding around on a table. 

These are going to be gifts for friends and family :) 
Full build tutorial: https://www.instructables.com/id/Sliced-Wood-Coasters/

Happy making!

transcript.text: Closed captions enabled automatically

Remove branches from a dead tree. 
Wood needs to be dry
I used branches from 0.5"-1.5" in diameter
Branches were sliced in a tabletop bandsaw to roughly the same length, about 0.5" thick
Height will be trimmed down later with a router used as a planer. However, getting the pucks consistent now makes planing easier
Randomly glue pucks to plywood,. Ensure some pucks overhang the edges, but leave one side open to use as a reference for the table saw fence.
I'm using regular wood glue here
After the glue has dried completely the plywood was cut into 3.5" strips, using the bare edge of the plywood as a straight edge guide on the table saw fence.
The overhang edge was trimmed first
#.5" wide cuts were made from the remaining board, moving the fence each time to keep the bare straight edge as a guide.
Here are the strips showing the irregular height of the different size pucks glued to the plywood
The strips were hot glued directly to the workbench to hold them in place while planing the tops down
Temporary rails were glued down on either side of the strips. These rails are taller than the highest point of the strip, allowing the router to pass over the top of the strip
The stock base plate of the router is removed, and a wide sled is attached to the mounting holes. The sled needs to be wide enough to transverse the rails without falling off.
Have the router fully retracted and make very shallow cuts into the strip, sliding the router along the rails.
Lower the router bit about 1/4" with each pass, slowly trimming the tallest pucks down.
Continue until all the pucks on the strip are the same height
Chip-out from being too aggressive
Remove strip
Hot glue can be chipped off back of strips with a chisel
After planing the router can leave milling marks. Use a coarse grit sandpaper to make a nice smooth top
Instead of epoxy, I used Teak Oil to stain and seal the end grain of the coasters.
Rubber feet bumpers were added to the underside to prevent the coasters from sliding around

summary.brief: A timelapse shows a woodworker cutting branches, gluing them onto plywood, planing, sanding, oiling and finishing wooden coasters.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a stack of finished coasters on a table beside two brown beer bottles while a boy in a red T‑shirt watches from behind a chain‑link fence under green trees. A man in khaki shorts and a white T‑shirt cuts dry tree branches with pruning shears and a handheld saw, creating short, uniform pucks. He randomly glues these pucks onto a sheet of plywood, allowing some to overhang and leaving one edge free as a reference. After the glue dries, he cuts the plywood into 3.5‑inch strips on a table saw using the free edge as a fence, then hot‑glues each strip to the workbench. Temporary rails are glued to the sides of each strip, and a router mounted on a wide sled rides the rails; shallow passes are made, lowering the bit each time until all pucks in a strip are level. The planed strips are removed, the router’s milling marks are sanded away with coarse then finer grit sandpaper, and the smooth surfaces are stained and sealed with teak oil. Rubber pads are affixed to the underside of each coaster to stop sliding. The finished coasters are displayed again, a can of beer is poured onto them, and the video concludes with a toy‑soldier figure holding a fork‑shaped head on a blue background.

action.detailed: Cut dry branches into uniform pucks, glue them onto a plywood board, plane the glued surface level with a router sled, sand the surface smooth, apply teak oil, and attach rubber pads to finish the coasters.

summary.brief: A woodworker timelapses the full fabrication of sliced‑wood coasters.
summary.detailed: The video begins with a long piece of wood being sliced on a bandsaw into thin, bark‑showing pucks. The pucks are arranged on a sheet of plywood, with some overhanging the edge, and small dots of glue hold them together. The glued strip is trimmed on a table saw using the straight edge as a fence. It is then mounted on a router sled with temporary side rails, and the router is run repeatedly, lowering the bit each pass until all pucks are planed to a uniform thickness. The surfaced board is sanded with progressively finer grits to remove router marks, brushed with teak oil for color and protection, and rubber pads are glued to the underside of each coaster. The finished coasters are shown being handled and used with beer cans.

summary.brief: A woodworker cuts, arranges, glues, sands, and finishes thin wood slices to create patterned coasters.
summary.detailed: The woodworker feeds dry branch slices into a bandsaw, producing thin bark‑edged rings that reveal the wood’s growth rings. The rings are laid on a bench, hot‑glue dots are applied to their backs, and thin wooden sticks are inserted with pliers to fill gaps, forming a mosaic‑like panel. The panel is measured with a tape measure and marked with a pencil, then trimmed to a uniform width on a table saw and repeatedly cut until all pieces share the same dimensions. A router‑mounted planer (used as a planer) and a sanding sled are run over the strips, leveling and smoothing them with progressively finer sandpaper. The leveled pieces are glued onto a plywood base; the four corners are reinforced with clear self‑adhesive stickers and rubber feet are attached to the underside. The assembled board is sanded again and brushed with teak oil to seal and colour the end grain. The finished square tiles are displayed as coasters on a table alongside cans of beer.

action.detailed: Cut the wood into thin rings, glue the rings together and insert thin sticks, trim the panel to size on a table saw, plane and sand the pieces to an even thickness, glue the panel onto a base, secure the corners with clear stickers, attach rubber feet, and finish the board with teak oil.

summary.detailed: In front of a house, a man wearing a white shirt, white shorts and white sneakers first picks up a fallen branch with dead leaves, then uses a hedge trimmer and a pruning saw to cut the main stems and smaller branches of a dried bush, stepping aside after each cut to push the severed pieces away and gather them; a cyclist rides past as he works around the plant, and after the debris is cleared he bends over to secure the leftover portion of the shrub to a large wooden log with a black rope, kicking the tied bundle aside while cars drive by.

action.detailed: Trim the dead shrub by cutting its stems and branches with a hedge trimmer and pruning saw, moving each cut piece aside, and then tie the remaining portion to a log with rope.
action.actor: a man wearing a white shirt, white shorts and white sneakers

nodes.plm_action: Cut tree branch using a handsaw
nodes.plm_caption: A man in a white shirt and shorts is bent over cutting some small branches from a fallen tree in the foreground. The tree has dead leaves. He is sawing in between the dead leaves and falls to the right as he saws off the branches. In the background, there is a house and bushes in the front, some buildings across the road and a bus. Cars are driving by. He then picks up the cut branches and throws them towards the left. He adjusts the fallen tree with his foot to a position horizontally across the tree, then adjusts the leaves around the branch. He then looks down on his hands and walks away, to his left, with his back to the camera. The video cuts to a circular saw cutting into the tree.

summary.brief: A man in a white shirt and shorts saws small branches from a fallen tree, clears leaves, and walks away as a saw cuts the wood.
summary.detailed: The man bends over the fallen trunk and uses a hand saw to cut off several small branches between dead leaves, letting the cut pieces fall to the right before picking them up and tossing them leftward. He places a foot on the trunk to hold it horizontally, adjusts the surrounding leaves, glances down at his hands, and walks away with his back to the camera. The shot then cuts to a saw (appearing as a table or circular saw) making another cut into the branch.

action.detailed: Use a hand saw to cut small branches from the fallen tree, pick up and toss the pieces, step on the trunk to hold it while adjusting leaves, then walk away as a saw finishes cutting the wood.
action.actor: a man wearing a white T‑shirt, shorts, and a white baseball cap

nodes.plm_action: Cutting log into multiple pieces using table saw
nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows the cutting of wooden logs into smaller pieces, cut in a tree pattern. The video cuts to the finished pieces at the end. A small, red, cut-out piece holds the log steady against the band saw blade. The pieces have a tree-look with visible bark edges and visible growth rings inside. The small cuts are made using a bandsaw and a miter saw.
The log is first positioned against the blade, with the pieces moving from right to left. The camera cuts at the beginning and middle of the video and then at the end. A piece of wood is used in the band saw to assist the movement while cutting the log. This piece is thrown onto the flat, white surface at the end of the video.

summary.brief: A log is fed into a bandsaw and cut into round discs that are stacked on the work surface.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with a brief table‑saw cut where the operator holds a piece of wood with both hands and pushes it past the blade. The view then shifts to a bandsaw: a small block is used to steady a short log as the operator pushes it from right to left against the moving blade. The blade slices the log into circular pieces that show bark edges and growth rings. The freshly cut discs fall onto a white tabletop, where additional slices are tossed onto the growing pile. Throughout the segment the operator continues feeding the log, producing a series of round slices that are later gathered and placed on a brown board.

action.detailed: Guide the log against the bandsaw blade using a small block, push it across the blade to cut it into round pieces, and collect the pieces on the work surface.
action.actor: A person’s hands operating the bandsaw

nodes.plm_action: Glueing sides down with wood glu
nodes.plm_caption: In this video there is a person sitting in the center of a table cutting wooden logs into smaller pieces. The person initially uses a tool to place two wooden pieces together, then they use pliers and a sharp tool to further divide the pieces. They then glue the pieces together to form a collage and set them in a straight line, as they measure the size they want to put them on before cutting them on a table saw.

summary.brief: A man glues small wood slices onto a board, trims them with pliers, then measures and cuts the board on a table saw.
summary.detailed: The video shows a man seated at a workbench. He first squeezes glue from a bottle onto the backs of many small round wood slices and presses each slice onto a larger wooden board, arranging them into a dense pattern. After the glued collage is complete, he uses pliers to trim or shape the ends of the individual pieces, turning them over as needed. He then measures the assembled board with a tape measure, marks the desired cut line with a pencil, and feeds the board through a table saw, pushing it steadily to trim it to the final size.

action.detailed: Apply glue to each wood slice, press the slices onto a board in a pattern, trim the pieces with pliers, measure the board with a tape measure, mark the cut line with a pencil, and push the board through a table saw to trim it to the desired size.
action.actor: A man wearing dark clothing, seated at a workbench

nodes.plm_action: Cut 2x4 pieces using a table saw
nodes.plm_caption: A speed up video of a person pushing pieces of wood across a table saw. The video ends with them preparing to glue up the pieces with a hot glue gun. Also in the background is a red electric drill with a white screwdriver. The person is wearing a ring on the left hand, finger.  and has fair skin. The wood is light brown with cut ends that are darker brown with many brown spots in between.

summary.brief: A woodworker slices light‑brown boards on a table saw, then lifts the strips and reaches for a hot‑glue gun.
summary.detailed: In a well‑lit workshop the worker pushes a light‑brown board across a table‑saw; the blade spins rapidly, cutting the board into thin strips that show darker cut faces and speckled grain, while sawdust falls onto the gray metal table below. A red electric drill with a white screwdriver is visible in the background, and the worker’s left hand wears a ring and has fair skin. After the fast‑forwarded cutting sequence, the same hands pick up four of the freshly cut strips, hold them up to display the grain and circular cutouts, and place the pieces on a workbench. The shot then cuts to another bench where two hand tools lie, and the worker’s hand moves toward a hot‑glue gun, indicating preparation to glue the strips together.

action.detailed: Push the board through the table‑saw blade to slice it into thin strips, then lift the strips, display them, and position the hot‑glue gun for bonding.
action.actor: the woodworker (a fair‑skinned person wearing a ring)

nodes.plm_action: Sanding to an inch with fine paper on a drum sander
nodes.plm_caption:
In a time-lapse video the process of creating wooden coasters using a sanding machine. He first cuts a board to size, then shapes the edges of the wood before drilling and sanding. Finally, he glues the wood and seals it with a protective coating. The coaster then falls through the air. The video was recorded at a table with a glister looking table top and a tool set is visible on the table. The wooden object is a light brown, the background table is tattered. There is one orange can with a blue and white label on the table.
The video begins with a close-up shot of a table with a grey and yellow pattern. In the background is a black and red glue gun, and a small white object placed on a black surface. The shot then changes, and a wooden board comes into view, as a hand with light skin, with short nails, holds the board. The shot changes again to a shot of the sanding machine, and then a hand takes over and a large square-shaped wooden board can be seen.
The video continues in a time-lapse of the process of creating wooden coasters. The coaster board comes into view as the hand pushes down and the tool presses down. As the camera focuses on the board, a small metal object is pressed against the wood and dust is collected, which is then pushed away. The tool comes back into view, and a piece of wood is pressed down. The sanding machine is moved over the wooden board, smoothing out the edges. As the camera pans over the board, the coaster comes into view.
As the video progresses, the coaster comes into focus from different angles and the camera is now out of focus. The coaster then comes into view at different sizes, as the camera pans back and forth. Finally, the coaster comes into view on the table in its final form. The camera then cuts, and the hand comes into view.
The table appears in close-up, as the coaster is shown on the table. The video ends, with a shot of a can of beer.

summary.brief: A woodworker planes, sands, oils, adds rubber pads, and displays the finished wooden coasters with beer cans.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with a close‑up of a patterned tabletop where a glue gun and other tools are visible. A hand positions a glued strip of thin wood slices on a router sled and runs the router over it, lowering the bit after each pass until the strip is uniformly flat. The stripped board is then run through a hand‑held sander to remove milling marks. After sanding, teak oil is brushed onto the surface to seal and color the wood. Small rubber foot pads are affixed to the underside of each individual coaster. Finally, the completed coasters are arranged on the table, and several beer cans are placed on top of them for the concluding presentation.

action.detailed: Plane the glued wood strip with a router on a sled, sand the surface smooth, coat it with teak oil, attach rubber foot pads to each coaster, and arrange the finished coasters on a tabletop with beer cans.
action.actor: the woodworker (hands visible performing the tasks)

nodes.plm_caption: An individual is using an electric machine with a blade to cut small flat wood shapes out of thick wood. They cut about ten pieces of wood. There are also shapes that haven't been cut but placed on a piece of wood, visible in the background.

summary.detailed: A man dressed in black works at a workbench covered with round wood slices, a white squeeze‑bottle of glue, and scattered tools. He dispenses a line of glue onto the back of each slice, places the slice onto a larger square board, and repeats quickly until the board is filled. action.brief: Glue wood slices; shape ends with pliers

nodes.plm_action: Cutting wooden pieces into smaller, precise pieces using a table saw
nodes.plm_caption:
In this sped up video of a woodworking process, a person is placing slices of wood on a wooden board. They use a pair of pliers to stick nails in each wood slice. They also use a tape measure and a pencil to measure the board. A table saw is used to cut the board. The person sits at a wooden table.
In the background, there is an orange machine, blue shelves, white, and a table that the board is on.

summary.brief: A woodworker arranges and glues circular wood slices on a board, then measures and cuts the board with a table saw.
summary.detailed: In a sped‑up view, the woodworker sits at a wooden workbench and places a series of small round wood slices onto a board, applying glue and using a pair of red‑handled pliers to drive tiny nails or pins that hold each slice in place. He adjusts the pieces, removes bark from some slices, and even positions a small white container in the center of the layout. After the assembly is complete, he pulls out a red tape measure, marks the board with a pencil, and then feeds the marked board through a table saw, guiding it with the fence until the board is cut into the desired shape.

action.detailed: Place the round wood slices on the board, apply glue, and secure each slice with a nail using the pliers; then measure and mark the board with the tape measure and pencil, and finally feed the board through the table saw to cut it to size.
action.actor: the woodworker, a man working at the bench

nodes.plm_action: Cutting individual pieces of wood using a table saw with a rip blade
nodes.plm_caption:
This video shows how the wood pieces are being sawn into multiple pieces. The video is in fast forward motion.
This video is set in a workshop. All the background is blurred as the camera is focused on the cutting machine, a piece of wood, and the saw blade. 

The cutting machine is being run through a piece of wood. It's hard to tell what shape the wood is cut into, as there are small pieces left over. There is a black and orange fence running along the bottom, with the saw blade in the middle. There are 6 small holes towards the bottom of the fence.

There is a white hand holding the wood in place, which is slowly moving forward towards the cutting machine. As the machine moves, the wood is being pushed into the machine, and the circular saw is spinning rapidly.

The wood is tan, with a lot of smaller cut ends on it, and larger ones in between. The saw is spinning around a lot, with the blade making a circle in the wood. There are a lot of small wooden pieces being produced as the wood is being cut through. The sound from the spinning blade can be heard, and the wood is making a little sound as it's being cut. The camera moves in very quick movements, so the scene is slightly fuzzy, and it's difficult to count how many times the wood is cut in order to cut it into different pieces.

There is a grey metal table underneath, that is not being used. The table is slightly sloped, and there are some sawdust particles around the sawing area.

summary.brief: A hand feeds a tan wood board through a table‑saw, producing many cut pieces, then a close‑up shows the slices being collected.
summary.detailed: In a workshop the camera follows a tan board with bark that is held by a hand and pushed forward across a table‑saw. The saw sits on a black‑orange fence marked with six holes, and its circular blade spins rapidly as the board is fed into it. The fast‑forwarded view shows the board being repeatedly pushed, the blade slicing it into numerous irregular fragments that fall onto a sloped metal table covered with sawdust. The scene then switches to a close‑up where the blade cuts the board more slowly, producing visible circular slices that pile up on the table, and the woodworker’s hand reaches in to gather the cut pieces.

action.detailed: Push the tan board steadily across the spinning blade of the table saw, guiding it with your hand (and a push stick) while the blade slices the wood into multiple fragments, then collect the cut pieces.

nodes.plm_action: Grab the wood

action.detailed: Hold the strips, turn them over to view both sides, place a strip on the bench among other pieces, and reach toward nearby tools.

nodes.plm_action: Apply thin layer of glue to back of each board

The individual picks up a brush to scrub at a piece of wood in front of them. They set the brush down and then pick up a glue gun and apply glue to a piece of wood that they have. The individual sets the glue gun down and puts the piece of wood on a table.
The individual then picks up two strips of wood and a wooden item, placing them on the table. They apply glue to the two strips and then to the wood. The individual sets the glue gun down and picks up a screwdriver before placing the strips on top of the wood.
The individual then puts a piece of wood on top of a black and silver tool, as well as a black cord. They use their hand to adjust the two pieces of wood and then press the tool down.
After this, the individual places the black and silver tool on a piece of wood. They pick up an orange and black tool and set it on the wood. They move the tool around and show how it moves the piece of wood in front of them.
After this, they pick up a silver and black tool and set it on a piece of wood. They adjust the tool slightly and use it on a piece of wood in front of them. The tool moves and grinds along the wood.
The individual uses another tool on the wood.

summary.brief: The woodworker glues several strips onto a board and then routes them to a uniform thickness.
summary.detailed: First a brush is used to dust off excess black spray paint from a wooden board. The worker then picks up a hot‑glue gun, applies a line of clear glue to the board, and places a strip of wood on it, tapping it into place. Additional strips are positioned on the glued board, more hot glue is applied, and a screwdriver is used to hold the pieces while they are adjusted against a black‑and‑silver jig. After the glue sets, the worker disassembles a router with a yellow‑handled screwdriver, reassembles it, and guides the glued assembly over the router base, lowering the bit in successive passes to trim and smooth the wood to a consistent height. The segment ends with close‑up views of the router cutting the wood while the operator’s finger guides the piece.

action.detailed: Apply hot glue to the board, press the wood strips onto it, secure them with a screwdriver, then run a router over the assembly, lowering the bit gradually to trim and smooth the strips to a uniform thickness.

nodes.plm_action: Glue the wood together
nodes.plm_caption:
A video of a person working on a wood-based artwork with small, cut wood pieces. There are tools and materials used for crafting used throughout. The video ends with the final product being held and then shown with the wood pieces cut in to small square-shaped tiles, being used as coasters on an outside table. In the background of the finished coaster are some empty soda cans.
The video has a time-lapse effect. The background is a wooden table with black stains. The colors are a variety of browns, blues and greens with a natural wood look.

summary.brief: Hands sand, oil, glue, and finish small wooden squares into coasters, then display them with cans.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a close‑up of the maker’s hands holding a router bit and using a small air blower to clear dust from round cuts on a flat board. A paintbrush is then used to draw vertical lines on the same board, and a wooden stick with a metal tip marks one end before the router is removed. A hand sander smooths the surface. Next, a rectangular piece of wood showing circular cut logs is worked with a chisel that carves and scrapes circles while glue residue is removed and the area sanded. An etching solution is applied to sharpen the circular design, followed by another sanding pass. After this, the maker glues a set of small square wood pieces onto a larger board, sands the glued surface, pours teak oil over the pieces, spreads it and wipes excess with sandpaper. Small clear adhesive dots are placed in each corner of the squares and the squares are bonded together to form finished coasters. The camera then shifts to an overhead view of three completed coasters arranged on a weathered wooden picnic table; a hand places three cans of beer on the coasters, showcasing the final product.

action.detailed: Sand the wooden pieces, coat them with teak oil, attach clear adhesive dots to the corners, glue the squares together, and arrange the completed coasters on a table while placing cans on top.

summary.brief: A man carves bark‑like patterns into a thin board with a black‑handled chisel, then scrapes a second board and lifts it off the bench.
summary.detailed: The video shows a light‑colored workbench where a long, thin piece of wood with circular, bark‑like cutouts is placed. The man picks up a black‑handled chisel and, in fast‑motion timelapse, draws the tool across the wood, cutting lines and removing material while a cloud of white dust rises. He continues the carving, using his left hand to steady the board and his right hand to guide the chisel, shaping the decorative pattern. The scene then shifts to a second board held flat; he uses a narrow‑bladed scraper with a black handle to scrape material from its surface, deepening the texture, and finally lifts this board off the bench, removing it from the frame.

action.detailed: Using a black‑handled hand scraper, the man pulls the tool across the thin board to remove material and form bark‑like cutouts, then lifts the board off the workbench.

summary.detailed: The segment starts with the woodworker applying a white, S‑shaped line of glue across a rectangular board using a flat metal tool held at about a 45° angle. The same tool is then used to lift and scrape the glue off the board, clearing the surface. A knife is briefly used to shave a small amount of wood from the piece. After the glue is removed, the woodworker picks up a corded yellow‑and‑black hand sander, steadies each of several planks that contain cut‑out circles with the left hand, and moves the sander back‑and‑forth across the surfaces, smoothing them to a uniform finish. The segment ends with a close‑up view of the now smooth wood.

action.detailed: Holding the board steady with the left hand, the woodworker scrapes dried white glue from the surface using a flat metal chisel held at about a 45-degree angle, then switches to a corded yellow‑and‑black hand sander and moves it back‑and‑forth across several wooden planks with circular cut‑outs, smoothing them to an even finish.

The camera then pans to show a black‑yellow screwdriver, a corded drill with a silver bit, and several stains on the work surface.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: sliced wood coasters
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
** No narration in this video. CC enabled to describe process. **

Natural wood beverage coasters made from thinly sliced tree branches. Stylish and fun to make, these coasters are a great addition to any home, and make great gifts!

Dry tree branches were chopped up on a tabletop band saw into small pucks, which were then glued to a thin sheet of plywood. The pucks were staggered and were glued to overhang the edge of the plywood on three sides, leaving the fourth side straight as a reference for the table saw fence. 

Once the glue had dried overnight, the straight edge of the plywood was re
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with a stack of finished coasters on a table beside two brown beer bottles while a boy in a red T‑shirt watches from behind a chain‑link fence under green trees. A man in khaki shorts and a white T‑shirt cuts dry tree branches with pruning shears and a handheld saw, creating short, uniform pucks. He randomly glues these pucks onto a sheet of plywood, allowing some to overhang and leaving one edge free as a reference. After the glue dries, he cuts the plywood into 3.5‑inch strips on a table saw using the free edge as a fence, then hot‑glues each strip to the workbench. Temporary rails are glued to the sides of each strip, and a router mounted on a wide sled rides the rails; shallow passes are made, lowering the bit each time until all pucks in a strip are level. The planed strips are removed, the router’s milling marks are sanded away with coarse then finer grit sandpaper, and the smooth surfaces are stained and sealed with teak oil. Rubber pads are affixed to the underside of each coaster to stop sliding. The finished coasters are displayed again, a can of beer is poured onto them, and the video concludes with a toy‑soldier figure holding a fork‑shaped head on a blue background.
action_list: Glue wood slices; shape ends with pliers
Apply glue and place wood slices
Chisel holes and insert wood pieces
Cut centers and insert white piece
Apply finish and attach corner protectors
